Superseded by PEP 634. This has come up before.

- PEP 637 ("Support for indexing with keyword arguments", 2020) proposed it; it was rejected, attributed to Python Steering Council. From the PEP: "At present keyword arguments are allowed in function calls, but not in item access. This PEP proposes that Python be extended to allow keyword arguments in item access." https://peps.python.org/pep-0637/
  The ruling: https://mail.python.org/archives/list/python-dev@python.org/thread/6TAQ2BEVSJNV4JM2RJYSSYFJUT3INGZD/
  It had been proposed before, in PEP 472 ("Support for indexing with keyword arguments", 2014, Rejected).
  It came up again in PEP 647 (2020, Final), whose rejected idea "Narrowing of Arbitrary Parameters" cites it: "This could involve the use of keyword indexing, as proposed in PEP 637." https://peps.python.org/pep-0647/#narrowing-of-arbitrary-parameters
  It came up again in PEP 696 (2022, Final), whose rejected idea "Allowing the Type Parameters Defaults to Be Passed to type.__new__'s **kwargs" cites it: "Ideally, if PEP 637 wasn't rejected, the following would be acceptable: T = TypeVar("T")" https://peps.python.org/pep-0696/#allowing-the-type-parameters-defaults-to-be-passed-to-type-new-s-kwargs

- PEP 472 ("Support for indexing with keyword arguments", 2014) proposed it; it was rejected, attributed to Guido van Rossum. From the PEP: "This PEP proposes an extension of the indexing operation to support keyword arguments. Notations in the form `a[K=3,R=2]` would become legal syntax. For future-proofing considerations, `a[1:2, K=3, R=4]` are considered and may be allowed as well, depending on the choice for implementation." https://peps.python.org/pep-0472/

  It came up again in PEP 637 (2020, Rejected), whose rejected idea "create a new "kwslice" object" cites it: "This proposal has already been explored in "New arguments contents" P4 in PEP 472: obj[a, b:c, x=1] # calls type(obj).__getitem__(obj, a, slice(b, c), key(x=1))" https://peps.python.org/pep-0637/#create-a-new-kwslice-object
  It came up again in PEP 647 (2020, Final), whose rejected idea "Narrowing of Arbitrary Parameters" cites PEP 637: "This could involve the use of keyword indexing, as proposed in PEP 637." https://peps.python.org/pep-0647/#narrowing-of-arbitrary-parameters
  It came up again in PEP 696 (2022, Final), whose rejected idea "Allowing the Type Parameters Defaults to Be Passed to type.__new__'s **kwargs" cites PEP 637: "Ideally, if PEP 637 wasn't rejected, the following would be acceptable: T = TypeVar("T")" https://peps.python.org/pep-0696/#allowing-the-type-parameters-defaults-to-be-passed-to-type-new-s-kwargs

A new proposal would need to answer the reasons above. People who know this history: Joseph Martinot-Lagarde, Stefano Borini, Steven D'Aprano.

why does python have vectorcall.answer: PEP 590 (Vectorcall: a fast calling protocol for CPython) is Final, written by Mark Shannon, Jeroen Demeyer. Its Motivation: "The choice of a calling convention impacts the performance and flexibility of code on either side of the call. Often there is tension between performance and flexibility." It set aside the approaches of PEP 580 and PEP 576 under "PEP 576 and PEP 580": "Both PEP 576 and PEP 580 are designed to enable 3rd party objects to be both expressive and performant (on a par with CPython objects)." (https://peps.python.org/pep-0590/#pep-576-and-pep-580).

This has come up before.

- PEP 3103 ("A Switch/Case Statement", 2006) proposed it; it was rejected. Its Rejection Notice: "A quick poll during my keynote presentation at PyCon 2007 shows this proposal has no popular support. I therefore reject it." https://peps.python.org/pep-3103/#rejection-notice

In the context of `match` statement this is technically also possible for matches against literal patterns." https://peps.python.org/pep-0622/#use-dispatch-dict-semantics-for-matches
  PEP 622 was later superseded by PEP 634.

A new proposal would need to answer the reasons above. People who know this history: Brandt Bucher, Daniel F Moisset, Guido van Rossum, Ivan Levkivskyi.
